sections.section_title: The Final Instruction of the Household Code -- Masters
sections.summary: Masters are commanded to provide justice and fairness to their slaves, knowing that they too have a Master in heaven. The instruction completes the household code (3:18-4:1) by subjecting the earthly master's authority to the heavenly Master's oversight. Its primary concern is the ethical treatment of slaves rather than the permanence or conditionality of the believer's standing before God.

sections.section_title: Prayer -- Persistence, Alertness, and the Open Door
sections.summary: Paul commands the community to devote themselves to prayer, keeping alert with thanksgiving. He asks them to pray for an open door for the word so that he may speak the mystery of Christ clearly, for which he is in prison. The section concerns the community's prayer life and Paul's apostolic mission rather than the question of whether the believer's standing is permanent or conditional.

The community is to walk in wisdom toward outsiders, making the most of every opportunity. Their speech is to be gracious and seasoned with salt, so that they know how to respond to each person. The section addresses the community's engagement with the non-believing world rather than the permanence or conditionality of standing before God.

sections.section_title: The Letter Carriers -- Tychicus and Onesimus
sections.summary: Tychicus, described as a beloved brother, faithful minister, and fellow servant in the Lord, is sent to inform the Colossians of Paul's circumstances and encourage their hearts. He is accompanied by Onesimus, identified as a faithful and beloved brother who is one of their community. Together they will report on everything at Paul's location.

Greetings are sent from six co-workers: Aristarchus (fellow prisoner), Mark (cousin of Barnabas, to be welcomed), Jesus called Justus (these three are the only Jewish believers among Paul's current co-workers), Epaphras (who always strives in prayer for the Colossians to stand perfect and fully assured in all the will of God, and labors earnestly for them and for those in Laodicea and Hierapolis), Luke (the beloved physician), and Demas. The section's primary function is personal greetings and network-building within the body of Christ, though Epaphras's prayer in v.12 -- that they may 'stand perfect and fully assured in all the will of God' -- echoes Paul's own prayer (1:9) and mission (1:28) and implies that standing perfect is a goal requiring ongoing intercession, not a status already irrevocably secured.

sections.section_title: Instructions for the Lycus Valley Network and Archippus
sections.summary: Paul directs the Colossians to greet the brothers in Laodicea and Nympha and the church in her house. He instructs that this letter be read also in the Laodicean church, and that a letter coming from Laodicea be read in Colossae. Archippus is told to take heed to the ministry he received in the Lord and to fulfill it (pleroo -- the same 'fullness' vocabulary that runs throughout the letter). The section concerns the regional network of communities and an individual's ministry commission rather than the permanence or conditionality of standing before God.

Paul writes the greeting in his own hand, asks them to remember his imprisonment, and closes with 'Grace be with you.' The closing grounds the letter's theological claims in personal cost (Paul writes from chains) and summarizes the letter's message in a single word: grace. The section is a personal closing rather than an argument about the permanence or conditionality of standing before God.
